root_cause.text: In the bnxt_re RDMA driver, three generic hardware counters were mistakenly placed after the `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR` boundary marker in `enum bnxt_re_hw_stats`, so `hw_stats` was allocated with `BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS` and `bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()` wrote past the end of the array.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR`, and `BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS` from after `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR` to before it, and the commit message states that `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR` is used as a boundary for allocating hardware statistics and that this placement caused an out-of-bounds write in `bnxt_re_copy_err_stats()`.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add new hardware statistics counters for request CQE, response CQE, and remote access errors.
intent_record.what: Three new enum values were added to `enum bnxt_re_hw_stats`: `BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR`, and `BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS`, inserted before `BNXT_RE_OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR`.
intent_record.how: This expands the set of hardware statistics identifiers the driver can track or expose, allowing additional completion queue error and remote access error counters to be represented at runtime.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove obsolete extended hardware stat enumerators from the bnxt_re stats list.
intent_record.what: Three enum entries were removed from `enum bnxt_re_hw_stats`: `BNXT_RE_REQ_CQE_ERROR`, `BNXT_RE_RESP_CQE_ERROR`, and `BNXT_RE_RESP_REMOTE_ACCESS_ERRS`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, these hardware stat identifiers will no longer be part of the enumerated stats set, so any code that iterates over or indexes extended counters will no longer include these error counters.

relevance_review.reason: The change adds hardware stats counters in the same enum area implicated by the bug. Since the root cause was misplaced generic counters after the boundary marker, adding request/response CQE and remote access error counters is directly related to the stats enum layout and the out-of-bounds allocation/copy issue.

The root cause is an out-of-bounds write caused by misplaced generic hardware counters after the OUT_OF_SEQ_ERR boundary, leading to incorrect hw_stats sizing. This change removes obsolete extended stat enumerators, which is a cleanup unrelated to the boundary/array-allocation bug.

candidates.rationale: This boundary marker was used to define BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS, but the three generic hardware counters were mistakenly placed after it. That made the standard counter array too small and allowed bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() to write past the end.

vuln_statements.explanation: This enum boundary marker defined BNXT_RE_NUM_STD_COUNTERS. Because the three generic hardware counters were added after this marker, the standard counter array was allocated too small, enabling bnxt_re_copy_err_stats() to write out of bounds.
